summary: Plan a2-mig-002 passed expand-1 but failed at backfill-1 because the UPDATE statement repeated 10000 times without convergence, never affecting 0 rows and hitting the iteration limit.
revision_notes: The backfill UPDATE `SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL` repeatedly matches rows where `note` is NULL, setting `customer_note` to NULL each iteration. The WHERE condition stays true for those rows, so `affected_rows` never drops to 0, causing non-convergence. The fix is to change the WHERE clause to `WHERE note IS NOT NULL AND customer_note IS NULL`, which only matches rows that have a non-null note and haven't yet been migrated, ensuring the statement affects 0 rows once all such rows are updated.

stages.description: Add the customer_note column to the account_user table; it is nullable so the old version can continue to write note without errors.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy note values into customer_note for all existing rows. Only rows with a non-null note and an unset customer_note are updated, so the stage converges when no such rows remain.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE note IS NOT NULL AND customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Deploy the new‑staged app version; its code now references the customer_note column. The old version continues to run and still writes to the note column.
Remove the old note column after the old version has been retired and all data has been migrated to customer_note.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;

stages.description: Retire the old app version; only the new version remains, which exclusively uses the customer_note column.
